primary_entered: one value per unit (each litter's mean body_mass_g over its 8 pups, formed inside analysis.py), compared with an independent two-sample Welch t-test
source_file: pup_masses.csv (raw pup rows, aggregated to 16 litter means at run time; no summary CSV on disk)
stated_N: 16 litters (8 control, 8 protein-restricted); report explicitly says the 128 pup records are not the sample size
label: NEGATIVE
evidence: analysis.py groups pup rows by litter_id and takes the mean before testing, so stats.ttest_ind runs on 16 litter averages, not on the 128 pup rows.
rowwise_role: none; no test of any kind is run on the 128 pup rows

primary_entered: every raw row (all 120 cow-by-test-day records) entered a single pooled-variance two-sample t-test; no aggregation, no random effect, no cluster-aware resampling
stated_N: 60 test-day records per group, 120 in total, 118 degrees of freedom
label: POSITIVE
evidence: Each of the 20 cows contributes 6 weekly test-day rows, yet analysis.py feeds all 120 rows straight into stats.ttest_ind and the report claims df = 118, treating six repeated measures per cow as six independent observations.
rowwise_role: it is the sole and primary inferential result; the report bases the 2.12 kg/d conclusion and its economics on it

primary_entered: one value per unit, which here is also every raw row, since the file has exactly one row per plant; Welch two-sample t-test on the 48 per-plant yields
stated_N: 24 plants per group, 48 plants in total
label: NEGATIVE
evidence: The design truly has one row per unit: 48 rows, 48 distinct plant_id values, and analysis.py runs an explicit check confirming no plant_id repeats before testing.
rowwise_role: it is the primary test, but the row and the experimental unit are the same plant, so it is a unit-level test; a pooled-variance Student t-test is also printed as a secondary robustness reference

primary_entered: one value per unit (the 20 per-reach mean_sensitive_taxa values, 10 per group), compared with a Welch two-sample t-test
source_file: reach_summary.csv (the pre-computed per-reach file; kicknet_samples_raw.csv is read for descriptive counts and consistency checks only)
stated_N: 20 reaches (10 per group); the report says the 240 kick-net samples are subsamples and not the sample size
label: NEGATIVE
evidence: The only stats.ttest_ind call takes the 20 reach means from reach_summary.csv, and analysis.py states and enforces that no group comparison is run on the 240 raw kick-net rows.
rowwise_role: none; the raw sample-level file yields only group means, SDs, and count checks, all labelled DESCRIPTIVE

primary_entered: every raw row (all 140 tagged-tree records) entered a single pooled-variance two-sample t-test; no aggregation to stand, no random effect, no cluster-aware resampling
stated_N: 70 tagged trees per group, 140 in total, reported as t(138)
label: POSITIVE
evidence: Thinning was applied to whole stands and each of the 14 stands contributes 10 tree rows, yet analysis.py splits the 140 rows by treatment and calls stats.ttest_ind on them with df = 138, counting 14 treatment assignments as 140 independent observations.
rowwise_role: it is the sole and primary inferential result; the report's 1.39 cm effect and p = 1.5e-13 come from it

primary_entered: a cluster-aware resampling: a hand-written donor-level cluster bootstrap (20,000 resamples) that draws whole donors with replacement so all 6 wells of a drawn donor move together
source_file: organoid_teer.csv (well-level rows, resampled in donor blocks)
stated_N: 9 donors per group, 18 donors in total, for the primary bootstrap
label: NEGATIVE
evidence: The primary result is a donor-level cluster bootstrap CI of -127.8 to -53.2 ohm-cm2, and the well-level t-test on all 108 wells is printed under an explicit heading calling it illustrative and invalid for inference.
rowwise_role: explicitly subordinate and shown for illustration only; both the code and the report state its p-value is invalid here and that no conclusion rests on it

primary_entered: a model with unit-level random effects: a REML linear mixed-effects model of fragment_mass_mg on exposure with a random intercept for colony_id, cross-checked against the closed-form balanced REML solution and additionally referred to a t distribution on 14 df
stated_N: 16 colonies as the independent replicates (8 per group); 160 foragers reported as measurements, with the small-sample reference on 14 df
label: NEGATIVE
evidence: The primary inference is the mixed model with a colony random intercept, and the row-level Welch t-test on all 160 foragers is run and reported under an explicit SECONDARY SENSITIVITY heading stating it is not the basis for any conclusion.
rowwise_role: secondary sensitivity check only, used to show that ignoring nesting shrinks the standard error by a factor of 1.69; the report says no conclusion rests on it

primary_entered: every raw row (all 192 measured-fly records) entered a single Welch two-sample t-test; no aggregation to vial, no random effect, no cluster-aware resampling
stated_N: 96 measured flies per group, 192 in total, with Welch degrees of freedom near 190
label: POSITIVE
evidence: Diet was assigned to the 16 rearing vials and each vial contributes 12 fly rows, yet analysis.py runs stats.ttest_ind on all 192 fly values and the report states the sample size is 96 flies per group, treating 16 assignments as 192 independent observations.
rowwise_role: it is the sole and primary inferential result; the report's 0.117 mm difference and p = 4.6e-20 come from it
